title: One-step correspondence for memory instructions
statement: Let $A$ be a program with memory instructions, and suppose its instruction at state $l$ is a memory instruction. For any oracle, input word, decider, initial decider states, register values, Boolean memory tape, memory-head position, and output word, there are a state $l'$, a Boolean memory tape $M'$, and a memory-head position $p'$ such that one program step from $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$ with memory $(M,p)$ gives $((l',v,\mathrm{none}),(M',p'))$, and one compiled-machine step from the corresponding seam configuration gives the seam configuration for $l',v,M',p'$, with the output unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction of $A$ at $l$ is a memory instruction.
